title: Phrases and clauses
goal: Join two short ideas into one longer sentence
intro: A phrase is a group of words without its own subject and verb (“in the morning”). A clause has its own subject and verb (“when I woke up”). Good speakers join clauses with words like because, when, and, but, so that their ideas flow instead of coming out as many short pieces.

rules.rule: A phrase adds detail: where, when, how.
A clause has its own subject and verb.
Join two clauses with one joining word, not two.
examples: I was late because the bus didn’t come.
Although it rained, we went out.

mistakes.wrong: Because I was tired. So I slept early.
mistakes.right: I slept early because I was tired.
mistakes.why: “Because I was tired” is only half a sentence. Join it to the main clause.

mistakes.wrong: Although it was late, but we continued.
mistakes.right: Although it was late, we continued.
mistakes.why: Use one joining word: although OR but, never both.

mistakes.wrong: Since I was sick so I stayed home.
mistakes.right: Since I was sick, I stayed home.

mistakes.wrong: The man he called me yesterday.
mistakes.why: Don’t repeat the subject with “he” or “she”.

ex.q: ___ it was raining, we played outside.
I stayed home ___ I had a fever.

ex.y: Don’t repeat the subject: My friend lives in Delhi.

ex.q: She was tired, ___ she kept working.
ex.y: “But” shows a contrast between two full clauses.

ex.q: Although he is rich, but he is not happy.
ex.fixed: Although he is rich, he is not happy.
ex.y: Use only one joining word: Although he is rich, he is not happy.

ex.q: Because the traffic was bad so I came late.
ex.fixed: Because the traffic was bad, I came late.

ex.q: My neighbour she is a doctor.
I called you ___ I needed some help.

ex.a: We went home early because it was raining.

ex.q: Join these with “because”: “I took a taxi. I was late.”
a: I took a taxi because I was late
ex.y: Main idea first, then because + reason.

talk: Talk about a day when something went wrong. Join your ideas with because, but, although, and when, instead of saying many short sentences.
